title: Per-rung sources, truncation-order analysis, and open questions for the Q_beta precision ladder
html:
Remark. Per-rung sources, truncation-order analysis, and open questions for the Q_beta precision ladder

Superseded by the Habiro-ring identification. The per-rung c_k coefficients below are the Taylor expansion of the EXACT, FINITE Habiro sum Σ_{m=0}^{M} a_m(u) · (u;u)_m with a_m ∈ ℤ[u] and M = 8 (proton/neutron). The precision ladder was useful when the closed form was unknown; now that the Habiro identification is established, the exact evaluation is used (no rung-by-rung truncation). See prop:habiro-precision-ladder-equivalence.

The content below is retained for HISTORICAL reference and for the derivation narrative (it shows how the pattern was discovered).

Per-rung categorical sources

See Table 1.

The categorical primitives are two:

  • Kashiwara b(q) = \sqrt{q^4+q^2+1}/(q^2+1) — Hoefsmit off-diagonal coupling on V_{(2,1)}.
  • Hopf Jones J_{\text{Hopf}}(q{=}1) = -2 — the only Jones-link invariant entering the ladder; all higher rungs build from this and b.

Mixing pattern across rungs:

  • c_1, c_2: pure Kashiwara (no Jones).
  • c_3: pure Jones (no Kashiwara).
  • c_4: multiplicative Jones \times Kashiwara mixing (c_3 \cdot b^4).
  • c_5: Kashiwara b^2 plus a half-Hopf offset, mixed intra/inter block (-(b^2 + 1/2)).

Two supersessions, in order. The earlier c_4 = b^2 + 1/2 form is superseded: it is 9.5% off the empirical value, while c_3 \cdot b^4 matches to 0.9%. The expression b^2 + 1/2 was then reassigned to the c_5 slot, carrying its categorical reading with it. The earlier c_5 = c_3^2 \cdot 3 + b = +12.87 form is in turn superseded: the SDP extraction gives c_5 = -1.2229, from which -(b^2 + 1/2) = -1.2527 is 2.4% away while +12.87 is an order of magnitude away and of the opposite sign.

The KL decategorification governs the appearance of classical-limit Jones values: the mass observable lives in the KL classical limit of the Hecke / quantum-group representation theory, so Jones invariants enter at q = 1 rather than at substrate q_0.

Truncation order and error estimate

The ladder is a convergent series: N is a truncation order chosen by the target precision, not an all-or-nothing canonicity decision. The ladder step is

u \;=\; b\,\hbar_q^2 \;\approx\; 0.00852, \qquad
  \frac{1}{u} \approx 117, \qquad \log_{10}\!\frac{1}{u} \approx 2.07,

so each rung gains \approx 2.07 decimal digits. The truncation error after N rungs is the standard first-dropped-term bound

\varepsilon_N \;\approx\; \bigl|c_{N+1}\,u^{N+1}\bigr|,

and the required order for relative precision \varepsilon is

N \;\geq\; \frac{\log_{10}(1/\varepsilon)}{\log_{10}(1/u)} - 1
  \;\approx\; \frac{\log_{10}(1/\varepsilon)}{2.07} - 1.
target N required
100\times experimental (7.8 ppb) 3
1 ppb 4
1 ppt 5
1 ppQ (10^{-15}) 7

Coefficient tier (read with the truncation order). The c_k carry a provenance tier: c_2 = -1 is structural — the exact u^2 coefficient of the explicit-factor product \prod_{k\ge2}(1 + c_k u^k), hence trivially q_0-independent. It is not proved: the Lean re-reads the N{=}2 factor rather than deriving it. And it is Taylor-exact for that series — the normalised series (cosine factor inside) has \tilde c_2 = c_2 - 1/8 = -9/8; c_k for k \geq 3 are at present structural near-matches — their empirical value swings with the q_0 anchor (e.g. c_3: -2.010 at the muon-pin q_0, -2.069 at the m_p-pin q_0), so they are not yet Taylor-exact derivations. A near-match that beats the experimental target is a genuine result and not a derivation. The permanent upgrade is to identify the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta Habiro element whose Taylor coefficients are the c_k — the same machinery that made the \alpha_{EM} next-order factor [2]_q(1-h^2\alpha) binomial-exact (prop:em-coupling-bring-zero-mode).

canonical precision ladder

Verified at q_0 via the canonical formalism at 50 dps:

See Table 2.

The N=4 rung is the first to beat the 7.80 ppb 100\times experimental target (CAL-3 σ = 0.78 ppm) — with c_3 at tier near-match (see the truncation-order section above). N=3 lands at 13.15 ppb, above that target. The signed column is strictly decreasing at both documented pins: with the live c_5 = -(b^2 + 1/2) every rung factor 1 + c_k u^k has c_k < 0 and is therefore below 1. That is not what the non-monotonicity claim is about, and an earlier draft of this paragraph got it backwards. The claim concerns the residual magnitude — whether the approximation gets worse — and on magnitude the signature survives, and survives only under the live coefficient. At the proton pin:

N \lvert\text{residual}\rvert, live c_5 \lvert\text{residual}\rvert, superseded c_5
4 6.1698 ppb 6.1698 ppb
5 6.2260 ppb (increases) 5.5551 ppb (decreases)

So the N{=}4 \to N{=}5 non-monotonicity is produced by the live c_5 = -(b^2+1/2) and is absent under the superseded +12.87 — the reverse of what the earlier draft asserted, which read the signed column where -6.1698 \to -6.2260 is decreasing. The ladder does carry a numerical signature of its own inexactness, now on the correct coefficient for the first time.

Caveat: the crossing is only 0.91\,\%, computed with c_3 at the recorded proton extraction and at the proton pin alone, so it is not robust to a large c_3 move; a full settlement re-extracts c_3 at both pins. The near-match tier of c_{k\geq3} rests independently on the q_0-anchor swing recorded above and does not depend on this crossing. Agreement at q_0 is research-grade and conditional on the Habiro-element upgrade, not an unconditional derivation.

The N=2 slight over-ceiling reflects that the Kashiwara-only prediction gives b^2 (= 0.7527) rather than the exact empirical 0.7656 — the 1.7% gap accumulates to the 0.28 ppm over-shoot. The N=3 Hopf correction absorbs this and brings the residual under the c(K) ceiling.

Implication for \Delta S (n−p mass split, 1 ppb)

From the canonical formalism:

  \varepsilon_{\Delta S} \;=\; \frac{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta}{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta + m_e} \cdot \varepsilon_Q
  \;\approx\; 0.605 \, \varepsilon_Q.

See Table 3.

At N=3 the n−p mass-split residual is 7.96 ppb, above the 4.74 ppb 100\times-experimental Δm_pn target; N=4 is the first rung below it, at 4.35 ppb, with N=5 taking off a further 0.03 ppb. The chain does not reach sub-ppb precision on this observable at either documented pin — an earlier draft of this paragraph claimed it did, on the superseded column.

Open

Extending the categorical treatment to all c_k reduced c_4, c_5 to closed forms in the two categorical primitives b (Hoefsmit Kashiwara) and c_3 = -2 (Hopf Jones at q{=}1), with sub-percent empirical match. The remaining open questions:

  1. Why c_4 = c_3 \cdot b^4? The multiplicative Jones \times Kashiwara mixing has no derived categorical proof yet. Suggested source: spectral-sequence stratification of the Wedderburn-block cohomology of H_n(q).

  2. Why c_5 = -(b^2 + 1/2)? The Kashiwara b^2 plus half-Hopf offset is suggestive but not derived, and it is 2.4% from the SDP extraction -1.2229. The earlier c_3^2 \cdot 3 + b reading of this slot is superseded.

  3. Inductive closure for k \geq 6. No closed forms proposed. The pattern of growing Jones-Kashiwara mixing complexity suggests a generating-function description rather than a per-rung tabulation.

The full inductive ladder follows from a categorical source for the operator-valued generating function F(z, q) = \sum_k c_k(q) \cdot b(q)^k \cdot z^k — for instance the KLR canonical basis or a Khovanov–Rozansky spectral sequence.

Provenance of the tables

Tables 2 and 3 above are computed by qbeta_precision_ladder_n5.py at the muon-pin (CAL-2) q_0, in convention C, with c_4 = c_3 b^4 and c_5 = -(b^2 + 1/2). That producer is the first in the corpus to evaluate the boxed five-rung product itself: the block's previously declared producer, probe_q_beta_operator_valued_N3.py, stops at N=3, carries no c_5, and is not the generator of these tables at all — its own witness records \varepsilon_{N=1} = 674.83 ppm against the +73.80 ppm of the N=1 row, because its first rung is \cos(\alpha_{N=1}) rather than the boxed \cos(\alpha - b\hbar_q^2/2).

As previously published, for the record. The \varepsilon_Q column read +1677.5, +73.79, +1.24 ppm, then +6.02, -0.57 ppb and, at N=5, \sim 0 ppb in table 2 and +0.04 ppb in table 3; the headline residual was quoted as -0.0066 ppm. Three defects are corrected above.

The sign. The published headline was negative. It cannot be: \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^A sits 1677 ppm above CODATA and every live rung factor is below 1, so the ladder descends to CODATA from above and a negative residual requires overshooting zero. Over both documented pins and all four documented (c_4, c_5) assignments the most negative fifth-rung residual is +6.50 ppb. This is a scope-limited negative about the boxed ladder under those assignments, not a proved invariant.

The input epoch. The published \varepsilon_Q column sits 7.133 ppb below the recomputed one. A change of inputs shifts \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^A / \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{CODATA}} by one relative amount and moves every rung by it, so the N=3 row calibrates the whole column; applied to the recomputed column that single offset then reproduces the published N=2 row (to its three significant figures) and the published N=4 row (to -0.572 against -0.57) — the latter only with the retired c_4 = b^2 + 1/2, so the published N=4 number predated the c_4 supersession that its own label column already carried. The cause of the 7.133 ppb offset is not identified: it is not the stored Q_{\mathrm{AME}} (0.78233355931 against the present 0.7823334093099085, a 191.7 ppb gap in the wrong direction), and not the CODATA-2018 to 2022 m_e move (1.35 ppb).

The headline's magnitude. Under that same offset the published-epoch fifth-rung residual lies in [-0.63, +0.63] ppb across all four assignments, so -6.6 ppb is unreachable at the published epoch as well as at the present one. The published magnitude has no reproducible provenance in this ladder, and the recomputed value replaces it rather than being reconciled with it.
